methods.notes: A Valetudo robot serves HTTP on its own IP; GET /api/v2/ enumerates the available endpoints. MQTT autodiscovery also advertises it to Home Assistant.

device.manufacturer: Sören Beye (Hypfer) + community (vacuum vendors: Roborock, Dreame, Midea)
device.name: Valetudo (rooted robot vacuum, on-device REST/MQTT)
device.notes:
Valetudo is cloud-replacement software that runs ON a rooted robot vacuum (Roborock, Dreame, Midea). It intercepts the vendor firmware's cloud communication ("brain parasite") without replacing the firmware, and exposes a fully local web UI, REST API and MQTT — no vendor cloud. This is the canonical rescue path for de-clouding a working robot or reviving one whose vendor cloud is dying.
LOCAL SURFACE (on the robot's own IP):
  REST base /api/v2; interactive docs + live UI at http://ROBOT_IP/swagger/
  GET /api/v2/           meta-endpoint listing every endpoint + method for
                         THIS robot (endpoints are generated from the robot's
                         capabilities, so the set varies by model)
  PUT /api/v2/robot/capabilities/BasicControlCapability  {"action":"start"|
                         "stop"|"home"}
  Capabilities are named, e.g. /api/v2/robot/capabilities/
  PersistentMapControlCapability. OpenAPI schemas back the docs and validate
  every incoming request.
  MQTT with Home Assistant autodiscovery is also available.

Valetudo is deliberately NOT a feature-complete reimplementation of the vendor app; it exposes what the robot's firmware supports.

openness.notes: Valetudo itself is open source; it interposes on reverse-engineered vendor firmware comms. Rooting the robot (per model) is a prerequisite — dustbuilder builds images with Valetudo prepackaged and DNS patched.

upstream_docs.covers: The REST/Swagger/MQTT interfaces, supported vendors, and the rooting-essentials guide.
upstream_docs.title: Valetudo — documentation

credentials.notes: The local REST/UI can be given HTTP Basic auth; by default it is open on the LAN. No vendor cloud is involved.

factory_reset.effect: Reverting to stock firmware / re-rooting is model-specific and not covered here. Valetudo config is stored on the robot; a firmware reflash clears it.

methods.description: Root the robot per its model's documented procedure (often a UART shell or fastboot; dustbuilder builds a Valetudo image), flash the Valetudo-enabled firmware, then use the on-robot REST/MQTT locally.

steps.action: Root the robot per the model's rooting-essentials guide (UART/fastboot/dustbuilder).
Flash a Valetudo-enabled image (dustbuilder can prepackage it and patch DNS).
steps.expect: The robot serves Valetudo's web UI/REST on its own IP.

setup.notes: Valetudo requires the robot to be rooted first (method varies by model — UART/fastboot/dustbuilder). dustbuilder can prepackage Valetudo and patch DNS. After rooting, Valetudo serves its local REST/MQTT with no cloud. The rooting steps are model-specific and not transcribed here.

rejoin.notes: Valetudo has a Wi-Fi configuration surface; the robot's network can be changed from the local UI without re-rooting.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The /api/v2 REST base, the Swagger UI, MQTT with HA autodiscovery and the capability model are from valetudo.cloud and the project's discussions/issues.
